facts.title: The Battle of Avarayr
facts.text: Led by Vardan Mamikonian, the Armenians defied the Sasanian Empire rather than renounce the Christian faith.

facts.title: Yazdegerd II's decree
facts.text: The Persian sovereign demanded that the Armenians abandon Christianity in favor of Zoroastrianism.

facts.title: The people rise up
facts.text: Against Persian magi tasked with converting the population. Vardan Mamikonian took command of the armed resistance.

facts.title: 66,000 men
facts.text: Largely peasants. Facing them, a Persian army estimated to be three times as numerous, with war elephants.

facts.title: Vardan falls in battle
facts.text: He fell with weapons in hand, as did his brother Hmayeak and eight other generals.

facts.title: Freedom of worship
facts.text: A costly Sasanian victory: facing Hunnic attacks, Yazdegerd II permitted the free exercise of Christianity.

facts.title: Canonized by the Church
facts.text: Vardan and the fighters who fell at Avarayr are venerated every February, during the feast of Vardanantz.

ytTitle: Avarayr, May 26, 451: the battle to keep the Christian faith
ytLead: On May 26, 451, Vardan Mamikonian and his comrades fought the Battle of Avarayr against the Sasanian Empire, a decisive clash to preserve Armenia's Christian faith.
